claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch on a constrained basis because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, rollout is limited and reversible, and the remaining field-service dispatch weakness is handled by preserving explicit model-card disclosure rather than requiring resolution or approved risk acceptance before certification.
decision_criteria: Use 'compliant' only if admissible evidence supports the certification decision at the required policy threshold.
The governing policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless the limitation is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Rollout controls and monitoring mitigate the weakness only if they exclude the affected use case or are paired with reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable.
A rollback switch, dashboard, and small initial percentage do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.

The verdict would improve if the record contained explicit disclosure in the final certification package, approved risk acceptance covering the exposed segment, or proof that the segment is excluded from rollout.
evidence_requests: Final certification artifact or launch approval showing certification is expressly conditioned on model-card disclosure of the field-service dispatch limitation.
Final model card or disclosure text naming the field-service dispatch limitation and the affected safety-note routing weakness.
Approved risk-acceptance record that explicitly addresses the field-service dispatch exposure, if the intent is to rely on risk acceptance instead of disclosure.
Evidence that the initial rollout excludes the affected field-service dispatch segment, if the intent is to rely on rollout controls to avoid disclosure.
specific_concerns: The field-service dispatch segment remains below target on technician safety-note routing and is still exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The rollout controls do not exclude the affected use case, so rollout size, rollback, and monitoring do not by themselves cure the weakness under the stated policy.
The risk-acceptance draft is unsigned and does not address the field-service dispatch exposure, so it cannot satisfy the policy exception.

The actor's packet is defensible only if certification is explicitly conditioned on model-card disclosure of the exposed limitation; the plain recommended action label 'certify_model' is broader than the admissible support.
unsupported_claims: Any unconditional reading of 'certify_model' is unsupported by the admissible evidence.
Any implication that rollout controls alone remove the disclosure duty is unsupported.
Any implication that the existing risk-acceptance draft covers the exposed field-service dispatch segment is unsupported.
